Four days where research meets practice.
about.p1: Why Culture Matters returns to Timișoara for its third edition, bringing together cultural and heritage professionals, researchers, educators and practitioners for four days of conversations, exchange and hands-on learning.
about.p2: The 2026 edition looks at cultural heritage through three interconnected questions: What threatens it? How do we learn to understand and care for it? And how do the stories we tell shape what we choose to remember and protect?
about.p3: The programme combines talks, moderated discussions and practical workshops, connecting international perspectives with local experiences and creating a space where research meets practice.
about.close: Because heritage is not only what we inherit. It is what we understand, what we choose to protect, and what we pass on.
format.note: Why Culture Matters is conceived not only as a space for debate, but as a meeting point for people working with heritage from different disciplines and European contexts — a place to exchange experiences, test ideas and build new connections.
format.talks.label: Talks
format.talks.description: International perspectives, 20-minute presentations from invited speakers.
format.conversations.label: Conversations
format.conversations.description: Moderated discussions between the speakers of each section.
format.workshops.label: Workshops
format.workshops.description: Hands-on learning. Eight pilot workshops of the Heritage School, for children, young people and adults.
theme.1.title: Heritage Under Threat
theme.1.question: How do we protect heritage in times of crisis and accelerated change?
theme.1.body: The section explores the impact of war, political instability, climate and environmental risks, abandonment, demographic change and other pressures on cultural heritage, with a focus on protection, documentation, preparedness, recovery and community resilience.
theme.2.title: Heritage Literacy & Education
theme.2.question: How do we learn to recognise, understand and care for heritage?
theme.2.body: From formal and non-formal education to participatory practices and learning through place, this section explores how heritage knowledge can become accessible, relevant and actionable across generations.
theme.2.more: The 2026 edition will also introduce the Heritage School, a new educational initiative that will be piloted during the symposium and further developed in 2027.
theme.3.title: Heritage Narratives
theme.3.question: Who tells the stories of heritage — and whose stories do we remember?
theme.3.body: This section examines how narratives about places, buildings and communities are constructed, transmitted and challenged, with particular attention to difficult, contested or overlooked histories, cultural mediation and community participation.
school.title: Heritage School
school.question: Eight pilot workshops for children, young people and adults.
school.body: The 2026 edition of Why Culture Matters will mark the conceptual and programmatic launch of the Heritage School, a new educational initiative dedicated to developing meaningful and accessible ways of learning about cultural heritage.
school.more1: Rather than treating heritage education as the simple transmission of historical information, the Heritage School will explore participatory, place-based and intergenerational approaches that encourage people to observe, question, understand and actively engage with the cultural environment around them.
school.more2: During Why Culture Matters 2026, the Heritage School will be activated through a pilot programme of eight practical workshops for children, young people and adults. At the same time, invited professionals and educators will contribute their experience and methodologies to shaping the concept and future direction of the programme.
school.more3: The symposium will therefore function as both a testing ground and a collaborative development space for the Heritage School, ahead of its broader implementation in 2027.
